$schema_note: Build brief for an AI coding agent. Read 'build' first, then 'design' and 'motion', then render 'content' exactly as written. Positioning comes from docs/portfolio-brief.md (16 Nov 2026): C# / .NET and backend roles in Ireland first, data and ML second. Do not invent metrics, employers, skills or links.

build.styling: Tailwind CSS (design tokens as CSS variables in globals.css, mapped in tailwind config)
build.content_source: Copy 'content' from this file into /content/portfolio.ts as typed constants; components read from there, never hard-code copy.

requirements: Fully responsive; 16px side gutter on mobile, max content width 1120px
Semantic HTML, visible focus rings, alt text, aria-labels on icon links
Copy assets/arjun-portrait.webp to /public; render with next/image, priority, sizes set
Toggle and outline buttons must show readable ink text in their resting state, not only on hover (set explicit color/background; never rely on inherited button styles)

design.direction: Minimal retro-modern. Warm paper background, ink-black text, one punchy accent. Like a 70s technical manual reprinted today: generous whitespace, thin rules, monospace labels. Extra-bold modern sans gives it punch in key places.

display.use: Hero name, section titles, stat numbers, footer name
display.notes: Modern extra-bold grotesque with a slight retro character. Tight tracking (-0.035em), line-height 0.95.

accent_serif.use: At most one emphasis word per headline, in accent colour. Never for body or long text.

retro_details: Section numbers in mono: '01 / SOFTWARE DEVELOPMENT'
1px rules between sections and around cards (color: rule)
Very subtle paper grain overlay (SVG noise, 4% opacity, pointer-events none)
Tech tags as small pill outlines in mono
Hard offset shadow on hover instead of blur shadows: 4px 4px 0 ink
avoid: Serif for whole headlines (italic accent word only)

principles: Ease-out for entering, ease-in-out for moving; never linear for UI
Motion should explain or reward, not decorate; one hero moment, everything else quiet
prefers-reduced-motion: disable translate/scale, keep opacity fades at 150ms
Every animation must be skippable or finish under 1s after the first visit; nothing blocks reading or clicking

patterns.hero_entrance: Extra-bold name reveals word by word from below a mask (y 100% → 0 inside overflow-hidden lines), stagger 70ms; italic accent word arrives last with a 4° skew settling to 0.
patterns.section_reveal: whileInView once, amount 0.2: y 16px → 0, opacity 0 → 1, 500ms, children stagger 50ms
patterns.project_card_hover: Card translates (-4px, -4px) and gains hard shadow 4px 4px 0 ink; category colour strip on left widens 4px → 8px; arrow nudges 4px right. 200ms ease-out.
patterns.link_hover: Underline draws left to right via scaleX 0 → 1 (origin left), 220ms; on leave retracts to the right.
patterns.tag_hover: Fill with category soft colour, 150ms. No movement.
patterns.button_hover_press: Hover: translate(-2px,-2px) + hard shadow 3px 3px 0 accent. Active: scale 0.97, shadow removed, 100ms.
patterns.nav_active_indicator: Shared layoutId pill under the active section link, spring transition.
patterns.experience_timeline: Vertical rule draws downward (scaleY) as the section scrolls into view; dot per role pops in with scale 0.6 → 1.
patterns.stat_counters: Extra-bold numbers count up once on first view, 900ms ease-out.
patterns.cursor: Do not replace the system cursor.
patterns.intro_loader: First visit per session only: mono counter 000→100 in the corner (~900ms), then the paper panel slides up (translateY -100%, 600ms in_out) and the hero entrance starts. Skipped on reduced motion and on variant switches.
patterns.scroll_progress: 2px accent bar fixed at the very top, scaleX driven by useScroll + useSpring (stiffness 200, damping 40).
patterns.nav_link_roll: Nav link text is duplicated in an overflow-hidden span; on hover the top copy slides up and the second slides in from below (translateY 0 → -100%), 250ms ease-out.
patterns.section_heading_rule: Title rises from a mask, then a 1px ink rule draws across beneath it (scaleX 0 → 1, origin left, 700ms).
patterns.portrait: Grayscale. On load: clip-path inset(100% 0 0 0) → inset(0) reveal from the bottom, 900ms in_out. On hover: image scales 1.00 → 1.03 inside its frame and an accent offset frame slides from (0,0) to (10px,10px) behind it, 300ms.
patterns.tech_marquee: A single row of stack names in mono between hero and about, scrolling slowly (40s loop, CSS transform). Pauses on hover; each name turns accent on hover. Static wrapped list on reduced motion.
patterns.magnetic_cta: Primary CTA buttons drift up to 6px toward the pointer while hovered (spring stiffness 300, damping 20), snap back on leave. Desktop pointer only.
patterns.project_card_tags: On card hover the tech tags fill with the category soft colour in a left-to-right stagger of 30ms.
patterns.experience_expand: Each role shows 2 bullets; a 'More' toggle expands the rest with AnimatePresence height auto + opacity, 300ms; the plus icon rotates 45° to an ×.
patterns.variant_switch: Switching FULL STACK ↔ DATA SCIENCE: an accent/teal panel wipes across the screen (clip-path, 700ms total), the accent colour cross-fades, and sections re-run their stagger.
patterns.copy_email: Clicking the email copies it; the copy icon morphs to a check (scale 0.6 → 1 + opacity), and a small mono 'COPIED' chip rises 8px and fades after 1.5s.
patterns.back_to_top: Square ink button; appears after 1 viewport of scroll (scale 0.8 → 1 + opacity, 200ms); hover lifts with hard shadow.
patterns.footer_name: Huge extra-bold name in the footer; each letter lifts 6px on hover (spring), neighbours lift 3px.
patterns.page_load_order: Loader → nav fades in (200ms) → hero words → portrait reveal → stats count → marquee starts. Total under 2.2s on first visit, under 1s afterwards.
patterns.mono_label_scramble: Section numbers and eyebrows scramble through random characters for ~400ms on first view and on hover, then settle. Fixed-width mono so layout never shifts.
patterns.id_card_flip: About section ID card. Hover (or tap / Enter on touch and keyboard) flips it on the Y axis, 600ms in_out, to show basic details on the back. Reduced motion: cross-fade instead of rotate.

content.about: I trained as a mechanical engineer and moved into software, so I still think about systems in terms of inputs, tolerances and failure modes. For two years I built clinical data applications used across 200+ hospital sites, in a regulated environment where validation, audit trails and data integrity were requirements, not extras. I then finished an MSc in Data Science and Analytics at MTU with First Class Honours, and I want to keep building data-heavy backend systems, with a longer-term interest in computer vision. I'm based in Cork and open to permanent roles anywhere in Ireland.

projects.title: Medical Claims AI Platform
projects.summary: A full-stack web app for reviewing insurance documents and claims, with an AI layer on top.
projects.what: Upload insurance policy documents, ask questions answered from the document with page-level citations, and analyse claim files for risk through a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) workflow.
highlights: End-to-end ownership: PostgreSQL schema, ASP.NET Core REST API with JWT auth, React and TypeScript front end
RAG pipeline: PDFs split into page-tagged chunks, embedded and stored in PostgreSQL; answers use only the closest chunks and cite their pages
Rule-based risk engine flags high, medium and low risk claims from uploaded CSV files, with dashboards for documents and claims
Containerised with Docker and deployed on Azure Container Apps

image.alt: Screenshot of the Medical Claims AI landing page with the claim review workflow

projects.title: UAV Battery Anomaly Detection
projects.summary: Anomaly-aware energy prediction for drones, built on 162 real PX4 flight logs (922,895 rows of battery telemetry).
projects.what: Autoencoders trained on normal flights score abnormal behaviour by reconstruction error, with the alert threshold set from the training score distribution. The anomaly score is then fed into LSTM and XGBoost energy models.
highlights: Transformer autoencoder was the best anomaly detector: AUROC 0.767, AUPRC 0.652
LSTM was the best energy predictor: MAE 0.520 Wh, R² 0.848 across 5 grouped folds

projects.title: Semiconductor Manufacturing Fault Detection
projects.summary: Detecting rare fault events in heavily imbalanced manufacturing sensor data (SECOM dataset).
projects.what: Classification pipeline using PCA for dimensionality reduction and SMOTE for class imbalance, with k-NN, Decision Tree and SVM compared on precision and recall rather than accuracy.

projects.title: Geometrical Optimisation of an MR Damper
projects.summary: Magnetorheological damper geometry optimised with FEM and design of experiments.
projects.what: 2D axisymmetric magnetostatic FEM model; geometry optimised with response surface methodology and a Taguchi design of experiments. The selected design gave 498.5 N damping force at 1 A, and flux return thickness above about 8.8 mm brought no further gain.

figure.label: damping force at 1 A, selected design

Set up and maintained CI/CD pipelines with GitHub Actions and Docker supporting twice-weekly releases for a 20-person Agile team; wrote unit testing and integration testing suites and did code review for teammates
Ran root cause analysis on production incidents, tracing them through application logs, fixing them and documenting the fix
Built and maintained backend services and REST APIs in C# and TypeScript for clinical data applications deployed across 200+ hospital sites in India and the UAE
Designed PostgreSQL schemas and queries with validation and audit trails built into the data flow, to protect data integrity in a regulated environment
Developed Angular front ends for internal clinical workflows, working with clinical and business users to turn complex data into usable screens
Investigated production data issues across a multi-site deployment, found root causes and explained them to clinical and business stakeholders
Delivered the Kiniqaly application end to end as part of a six-person team, building in C# with Angular front ends and MongoDB
Trained 60+ junior engineers across three cohorts in programming fundamentals, object-oriented design and testing

items.title: Analytics MCP Server
items.summary: Model Context Protocol server that lets AI coding tools (Cursor, Windsurf, Zed) query live analytics data and generate dashboard code from it.
items.detail: Five MCP tools over stdio, backed by PostgreSQL raw and analytics schemas, dbt incremental models, a nightly Airflow DAG and Kafka event ingestion.

items.title: Pharmacy Sales BI Dashboard
items.summary: End-to-end sales analytics on pharmacy transaction data, from data quality checks to interactive dashboards.
items.detail: Python data preparation and revenue verification feeding Tableau dashboards for branch KPIs, product profitability, customer demographics, GIS mapping and Sankey payment flows.

items.title: Pill Defect Detection
items.summary: Visual quality inspection for pharmaceutical pills, trained on the MVTec AD dataset.
items.detail: Autoencoder flags defects by reconstruction error, evaluated with a precision-recall curve; Gradio interface with SQLite logging of each inspection.

items.title: Chest X-ray Anomaly Detection
items.summary: Convolutional autoencoder for pneumonia anomaly detection on the Kaggle chest X-ray dataset.
items.detail: Compared against a PCA reconstruction-error baseline and evaluated with ROC-AUC and anomaly recall.

items.title: Sensor Data PCA Studies
items.summary: Dimensionality reduction and clustering on real sensor data: smartphone activity recognition, wearable sports activity and gas sensor drift, plus a manual DBSCAN study.
items.detail: PCA, LDA, K-Means and DBSCAN with scikit-learn and NumPy.

items.title: Sarcasm Detection
items.summary: Custom Naive Bayes implementations with TF-IDF and numeric meta-features for detecting sarcasm.
items.detail: Text preprocessing, class imbalance handling and error analysis.

items.title: Tweet Sentiment Classifier
items.summary: Multinomial Naive Bayes written from scratch with Laplace smoothing.
items.detail: No ML library for the model itself: counting, smoothing and scoring implemented by hand.
